title: Module 15 practice assessment
description: This quiz is ungraded. Take it as often as you like, and read the feedback after each question, because the wrong answers are mistakes an agent or a student really made.

questions.prompt: In a clean clone of Chapter 4's project, a test run before `--import` printed seven `PASS` lines, exited 0, and logged 55 `ERROR` lines. The same step in a clean clone of `walker-jumpman-clawd` needed no import. What explains the difference?
choices: `walker-jumpman-clawd` commits its `godot/.godot/` folder, so every clone already carries the converted assets and the import cache.
Godot skips the import when every script has a `.uid` file beside it, and `walker-jumpman-clawd` commits one for each script while Chapter 4's project did not.
`walker-jumpman-clawd` is source-ready and Chapter 4's project is not, because a source-ready clone is one that needs no import step before its checks run.
`walker-jumpman-clawd` draws everything in code and has nothing to import, while Chapter 4's project loads textures and sounds that need the import cache.
questions.feedback: A project that draws everything in code has nothing for `--import` to convert, so knowing which kind of project you have is part of reproducing it; Chapter 4's project loads textures and sounds, which is why its pre-import run exited 0 while logging 55 `ERROR` lines ("The question", item 1). A clean clone never carries `godot/.godot/`, and `.uid` files are identifiers that an import generates, not a cache that lets Godot skip it.

questions.prompt: After the agent's first pass, all four test scripts passed, and its summary said no test touched the player's real save. Which evidence showed that claim was false?
choices: A clean clone's `git status --short` listed an untracked `best_time.json`, which showed the tests had written the save inside the project folder.
With `HOME` pointed at a scratch folder, the unchanged `test_game.gd` and `test_keyboard.gd` each wrote `best_time.json` into `user://`.
One of the agent's four `godot` runs exited with a non-zero code, and its summary reported all four suites as passing anyway.
`git diff` showed edits to `test_game.gd` and `test_keyboard.gd`, which the prompt had forbidden, so the old tests were saving to a changed path.
questions.feedback: The leak showed up only when the instructor ran the old suites with `HOME` redirected and looked in the scratch `user://` folder, which lives outside the project, so `git status` cannot see it. The old tests were not edited and all four suites passed: the gap was that they never set the new save path ("What the agents got wrong", first item).

questions.prompt: A save file with `"version": 2` and a renamed `"level"` was overwritten by the first-pass code on the next completion. What in the game's code caused this overwrite?
choices: `_load_best()` checked `format` and `level` before `version`, returned on the wrong level, and so never set the newer-build flag that blocks saving over the file.
`DirAccess.rename()` overwrites an existing destination, so the temporary-file write replaced the version-2 file whatever the game had decided about it.
`_load_best()` set the newer-build flag correctly, but `_save_best()` did not consult it and wrote the temporary file on every completion that beat the best.
The agent's own version-2 test case changed only the version number, so the combined case that renamed `level` was never exercised and the overwrite went unnoticed.
questions.feedback: The rule is to read `version` first and never overwrite a newer file, whatever else in it changed; the first-pass code checked `format` and `level` first, so the file looked merely invalid and was replaced. `rename()` does overwrite, but the game decides whether to save at all, and the agent's own version-2 case explains why its test passed, not why the code failed ("The ideas", section 4, rules 1 and 2).

questions.prompt: With no Godot 4.7.2 export templates installed, `--export-release "Web"` exits 1 while `--export-pack "Web"` exits 0 and writes a ZIP. What does the pack establish?
choices: That the Web preset is export-ready, because a package was written, `tests/*` stayed out of it and the command exited 0.
That the Godot 4.7.2 export templates are installed, because building a pack uses the same templates as a release export and would otherwise fail.
That it lists the files the preset would ship, as data only; the ZIP is an inspection listing, not something a player can launch as a game.
That nothing unintended would ship, because the ZIP's 20 entries included no file from `tests/` and the level JSON was packed.
questions.feedback: On 4.7.2 `--export-pack` needs no templates, so it can only list what would ship, as data. The instructor's ZIP held 20 entries, with nothing from `tests/` but the diagnostic gallery scene included, so a clean-looking listing is still not 'nothing unintended'. The failing `--export-release` is the real evidence that the project is not export-ready here ("The ideas", section 3).

questions.prompt: `node scripts/clawd-build.cjs` prints `Error: Invariant changed: godot/ui/hud.gd` after FEAT-10 adds a best-time line to the HUD. What is the right response?
choices: Remove `godot/ui/hud.gd` from the script's list of preserved files so the invariant check passes again and the build can continue.
Treat it as a design decision with an owner: decide whether the invariant should change, and record the reason in `CHANGE-BRIEF.md`.
Ignore the error, because all five Godot test scripts pass and a clean clone of the published commit already reproduced the committed `build_id`.
Revert the HUD change without comment and drop the best-time line, because the first iteration promised `godot/ui/hud.gd` stays byte-identical.
questions.feedback: The first Clawd iteration promised `hud.gd` would not change, and FEAT-10 changes it, so the script's complaint is accurate. Whether to update that promise is a decision for the project's owner, and it belongs in the written record; deleting the complaining line, ignoring it because the Godot tests pass, or reverting without comment all hide the decision ("Ship It").

questions.prompt: Which sentence about the FEAT-10 work is most defensible in a final film or submission note?
choices: In the cases tested, the save rules hold for missing, corrupt, newer-version and unwritable files, so a player's best time survives a crash between the write and the rename.
The Web preset is committed, `--export-pack` wrote a 20-entry ZIP and Godot found the preset valid enough to look for templates, so on this Mac the Web build is export-ready.
A clean clone of a named commit imports on Godot 4.7.2 and passes all five test scripts, so it is source-ready there; no export was built or played, and no screen reader was tested.
On the instructor's Mac the corrected suite passes 38 of 38 checks and the reviewer's check 13 of 13, so the complete panel's best-time line is verified as readable at 640 × 360.
questions.feedback: A claim is only as strong as its evidence. The clean-clone run supports 'source-ready', and the last clause names what it does not cover ("Verify" and the Walker example). A crash between write and rename was never tested, a pack listing plus a failed `--export-release` does not make a package export-ready, and no check looks at whether the best-time line fits the screen.
